decision.action: reject fixed unconditional expansion before construction and retain BM25
decision.reason: At window 1 the optimistic fixed-expansion ceiling is 840/2255 on a 21.7-chunk slate, while plain BM25 read to the same per-query slate size reaches 1041/2255. Expansion loses by 201 queries at equal cost with no control truncation. Windows 2, 3 and 5 lose by 271, 289 and 253 with understated controls. The fixed always-expand candidate was not built; paired expansion-only wins show that this result does not rule out a query-adaptive hybrid.

limitations: The expansion figure is an upper bound: it assumes expansion is free and that every reachable gold chunk is retained. A built candidate would score at or below it.
The budget-matched control is truncated at k=40, so it understates BM25 for 217, 838 and 1293 queries at windows 2, 3 and 5. Window 1 has no truncated query.
Complete evidence coverage is a retrieval endpoint. Larger slates cost generation tokens and carry lost-in-the-middle risk, which this record does not measure.
Canonical qrels identify the first fact-bearing chunk, so reaching a different chunk of the correct document earns no partial credit.
The slate-size curve is descriptive evidence about candidate budget, not a validated default; k must be selected from a generation-layer measurement.
Aggregate budget-matched losses reject fixed unconditional expansion, but expansion-only wins on 56 to 96 queries show that a separately preregistered query-adaptive selector is not disproven.

method.description: Compute the best attainable complete-evidence coverage of parent-document expansion directly from a baseline run, then compare it against the plain BM25 ranking truncated to the same slate size on the same queries.
